channel.title: TribeAwaken — Tony Skrelūnas
channel.description: Human resilience to cross hard ground. Ancient tools for future-proofing generations.

item.title: Why I Started a Magazine, and Why I Am Starting It Again
item.description: It began in 2021 under a different name. Five years later there are two novels out, a doctorate underway, and the same stubborn idea: that what a people reads every morning decides something.

item.title: Speak Only What You Want Built
item.description: My great-grandmother corrected careless speech the way she corrected a tool set down in the wrong place. Forty years later I understand why they were the same error.

item.title: Wanting Narrows the Eye
item.description: My grandfather never had money and was never poor a day in his life. Abundance turns out to be a question about perception, not arithmetic.

item.title: Stone Breath Has Gone Out to the World
item.description: Stone Breath has entered worldwide distribution: Apple Books, Kobo, booksellers from Berlin to Sydney. One universal link reaches all of it.

item.title: The Coach Who Borrowed the Circle: What Phil Jackson Was Actually Doing
item.description: Phil Jackson put silence, story and a circle into the most pressured organization in American sport and won 72 games. He had to borrow the pieces.

item.title: The Full Directory — Tony Skrelūnas
item.description: Every piece of writing at TribeAwaken, newest first, with its date and its stream.

item.title: The First Fire — three days in the redwoods, and the crossing that came out of it
item.description: About twenty people came to the meditation. What they got was not a meditation. It was a crossing with a destination, and at the far end they were expected.

item.title: The Winter That Didn’t Come — the method is right and the content has expired
item.description: A Sámi reindeer herder, taught properly and entirely correct, standing on ice. What to do when the knowledge itself is no longer true.

item.title: What a Far Messenger Is — and why we have to become one again
item.description: It is book four. It is the doctorate. And it is the thing I have been circling my whole life without knowing what to call it.

item.title: The Ground Is the Argument: Regenerative Agriculture and the Future the Council Fire Describes
item.description: I wrote a novel about what a people build after the extraction economy runs out. Then I watched farmers and Indigenous leaders build it, on real ground.

item.title: Stone Breath: Born on the Solstice, On Purpose
item.description: A novel about the songs we carry across oceans — and the roots that a lifetime of forgetting could never take. Released on the solstice, on purpose.

item.title: They Tried to Erase a Whole People. Now They Raise the Happiest Young Souls on Earth.
item.description: Book smugglers, song keepers, and a basketball team in tie-dye. The story of a people who were supposed to vanish and came back singing.

item.title: Tibet, and the Unbroken Thread
item.description: A people is not its territory — it is the thread: the language, the prayer, the way of raising children. Reflections from Machik Weekend in New York, and what the Tibetan community in exile teaches all of us about carrying wisdom across hard ground.

item.title: Twenty-Five Years to That Podium
item.description: I started this doctorate as an extension of my MBA more than twenty-five years ago. Last year I gave the PhD commencement address at Prescott College. Here is what happened in between — and what I found when I arrived a few days early.

item.title: What the Cottonwood Sings: A Poet's Afternoon in the Roots Workshop
item.description: In a gallery full of grief and color, a room of strangers became a circle. I picked up a pen for the first time and wrote my way back.

item.title: One in a Trillion: Five Days at Rancho La Puerta
item.description: Invited to Abundance Week at Rancho La Puerta to meet Tom Blue Wolf and Pat Mitchell — and the hour under the papel picado that came of it.

item.title: The Ancestral Code for Living to 100
item.description: Across the world, the peoples who reach a hundred are not lucky — they are living a code their ancestors wrote into food, movement, purpose, and song. We did not lose it. We stopped reading it.

item.title: The Machines That Could Help Us Come Home: AI, Robotics, and the Repair of a Warming World
item.description: A warming planet is asking hard questions. What if the intelligence we built to speed up extraction could be turned, deliberately, toward repair?

item.title: The Silent Theft: How the World Wastes Its Most Precious Resource — And How We Can Reclaim It
item.description: We track every barrel, every dollar, every ton — and let the one irreplaceable resource evaporate: human genius. This is the anatomy of a silent theft, and the map back to an honorable harvest.

item.title: The Final Council: Building a Post-Extraction Future for Economics and Technology
item.description: A recurring dream of a council that vets the future before it is built, and a blueprint for encoding reciprocity into AI, robotics and the next economy.

item.title: Seeds of the Ancestors: Remembering Our Food, Our Stories, and Ourselves
item.description: The blueprint for a sustainable future is not a new invention waiting to be engineered. It is an ancient inheritance waiting to be remembered.

item.title: Walking in Lightness, Eating in Balance: The Native Path to Long Life and Sustainable Health -Tony Skrelunas, PhD Candidate
item.description: Navigating the complex terrain between global economic systems and the specific needs of Indigenous communities has been the defining work of my life.

item.title: The Monster-Slayer's Blueprint: Turning the Age of Waste into an Age of Renewal
item.description: Every people on Earth descends from a line of monster-slayers. The take-make-dispose economy is the beast of our age, and the tools are older than it.

item.title: Weaving a New Dream: What Is the World Dreaming Through You?
item.description: We are taught to chase our own dreams. But there is an older, larger dream — the dream of the land itself — and it is trying to move through you. This is what it asks.

item.title: Hitting the Healing Trails with Navajo Humor
item.description: In the land where the sun kisses the earth, And the winds whisper ancient tales,

item.title: "The Warrior's Path"
item.description: Stepping out of grad school with an MBA and a vision to transform a nation, and what the years actually taught me about the warrior's path.

item.title: The Water Remembers: My Grandfather's Song at the Sacred Lake
item.description: My grandfather stood at the edge of a mountain lake and was called to sing an old song. What he taught me there: water has a memory, and so do we.

item.title: Facing the Changing Climate: Global Lessons & Navajo Strength
item.description: Ya’at’eeh, Relatives. As global temperatures rise, the way we cultivate food is undergoing significant changes.

item.title: Wealth Wisdom from the Sheepherders of the Planet
item.description: Across the herding peoples of the earth, wealth was never counted in currency but in flocks, dawns, clan bonds, and resilience that outlasts a drought.

item.title: Roots of Resilience: What the Fire Taught Us at Wisdom Week
item.description: Under the stars at Rancho La Puerta, elders and strangers became a circle. A week on how healing begins the moment we are truly seen.

item.title: The Wealth That Cannot Be Spent: Raising Generations Who Inherit More Than Money
item.description: The richest people I know own almost nothing a bank would recognize — and everything the great-grandchildren will need. A meditation on the wealth that is grown, not extracted, and passed down whole.

item.title: The Old Farmers Are Right: Ancient Agriculture as a Hedge Against a Warming World
item.description: Across the drylands of the world, a handful of master farmers still coax miracle harvests from wind and sand using knowledge older than any market. As the climate shifts, their methods may be one of humanity's best hedges — if we help the young stay to inherit them.

item.title: Shizhé'é: A Father's Day Letter to the Man Who Chose Me
item.description: A son's letter to the father who took him as his own — a city boy who followed love to the high country, learned the old ways, and became a pillar. A tribute to every dad who carries a family quietly on his back.

item.title: Honorable Trade: What the World's Oldest Economies Teach a Planet in Transition
item.description: For ten thousand years, whole continents ran on economies built not for shareholder wealth but for honor, love, and excitement. As the globe searches for a way through climate change, these time-tested systems hold a map — and it is not too late to read it.

item.title: Long Lives as modeled by our Ancestors - Hozhoogo Nizaadgoo Iina - We can live past 100 years again
item.description: TribeAwaken joins Northern Arizona University's Department of Health Sciences on improving the health and well-being of Native communities.

item.title: When motorcycling or any adventurous hobby beckons you to overcome fear and limiting beliefs
item.description: As a kid, I grew up in a modest traditional Navajo home far from the city and mainly with livestock and no electricity. A lot of times we would stay at sheep camp with grandparents all summer long and my cousin Alex would stay with us.

item.title: Time Tested Traditional Tribal Tools against the coronavirus
item.description: Many of you have questions about the pandemic and it seems the more you read and research, the more confused you get. What do we do to stay safe? What are the best ways to strengthen our immune system?How do we prepare if someone in our family, household, or we catch the virus?

item.title: In a Spa State of Mind. Unique world class resort-spas are thriving. What can we learn from them
item.description: What is a wellness spa? The word spa conjures up images of mud baths, soothing facials, relaxing massages, and rejuvenating body scrubs.

item.title: Our biggest Advantage inside is seeing from a Vantage outside
item.description: Inspiration from an interview with Gary Vaynerchuk, Entrepreneur and Author

item.title: A Magazine to Uplift Our Community
item.description: A Conversation with the Founder of “the Abundance Mindset Magazine” Magazine

item.title: From Sheep to the Customer: An Entrepreneur and her Food Business
item.description: Native Grill serves “Navajo soul food” to travelers along Highway 89 and to their loyal customers in Cameron, Arizona. Alfreida Littleboy and her mother started their business in 2013 and pursued their business license in 2016.

item.title: TribeAwaken.com Biker Review of the The Triumph Tiger 1200 XCA
item.description: The founder of TribeAwaken.Com, Tony Skrelunas, wanted to share his passion for motorcycles with others who may be inspired to also try out a bike.

item.title: "Buy Navajo, Buy Local" Conversation with Marvin Lizer, Navajo Nation Vice President
item.description: On buying Navajo and buying local: why keeping the dollar home in a community is economics, not sentiment, and what it builds when it stays.

item.title: A Seven-Point Tribal Review of Benefits from the National Economic Transition Platform for Tribes
item.description: Tribal communities such as Hopi, Navajo, and Crow are being impacted by the transition away from coal fired power generation to more economical alternatives. In northern Arizona, in Navajo and Hopi, many families were very proud to have a son or a daughter with a good-paying job from which many benefited.

item.title: To thrive, a business must pivot with care. Covid creates new opportunities for entrepreneurs
item.description: Our oral histories tell of times that almost destroyed our people. In every one, survival turned on the same thing: how carefully the pivot was made.

item.title: How do we keep our dollars in our community? Create good options to eat, shop, entertain, relax
item.description: Special to TribeAwaken to offer Economic Diversification Strategy to former coal and power plant communities

item.title: Inspiration for new types of grocery stores to improve our health and reawaken our "Blue Zone"
item.description: In the not too distant past, it was very common for many tribal elders to live to be over 100. In my Navajo culture, centenarians were celebrated and 102 years of age was a virtue to strive for and a blessing to bestow on friends and loved ones. This is why we use 102 yucca stems in our Winter Shoe Games.

item.title: Its ok to take the lead, rejoice in it, be grateful of your blessed abilities
item.description: As the founder of tribes.humans.net, it was a daunting task to pull all the pieces together. Talk about doing business all over the world, in big cities, working globally with investors, programmers, and experts. Working in different time zones and time clocks. To do it well and to take it this far, I had to go all in.

item.title: Exercise and the Many Benefits
item.description: The two do not sound connected, but working out serves mental health as much as physical, and the combination is the whole point.

item.title: 30,000 Years: A Message to the Graduates — Tony Skrelūnas
item.description: Tony Skrelūnas's commencement address to the Native American graduates of Northern Arizona University, on the great trade civilizations of the Americas.

item.title: What waking up early did for me and what it could do for you
item.description: What could waking early do for me and what do I hope to achieve in this tiny turnaround of life? Waking up early would allow me a more productive day, longer days, make me more successful in health and life, and maybe even make me feel better overall.

item.title: Extra, Extra, Read all about it: “We’re running out of sand”
item.description: “Sand, sand is everywhere”, take a few steps outside and there’s sand right below your feet. Oh, it’s concrete? Yeah that’s sand too. Your phone? Melted sand.

item.title: Did your ancestors have arranged marriages and what can we learn from that history?
item.description: What can we learn from our arranged marriages of the past in our modern day dating processes and eventual marriage of the right life partner? This article is to get conversation going.

item.title: The highest success takes discipline and a strong life partner while surrounded by temptation
item.description: What it takes to succeed under the kind of pressure most people could not handle, and the role a strong life partner plays in it.

item.title: Being tribal means ensuring the passage of cultural knowledge
item.description: The main meaning of being tribal is to completely engage in the value of ensuring that your kids, your relatives, your neighbors, your tribe succeed.

item.title: Helping Young Tribal Runners Achieve their Olympic Vision
item.description: The question that hasn’t been asked is “is it possible to support talented runners in a supportive tribal community setting? And how could it be done?”

item.title: Keeping the Tribal Dollar in our local communities while Honoring our Tribal Values
item.description: As a child growing up on the Navajo reservation at a placed called Big Mountain, I always looked forward to traveling to the Tonalea Trading Post.

item.title: 3 Pillars of Good Customer Service from a tribal perspective: Woshdee, Bahozho, K'enidzin
item.description: Great customer service is good business and good for our culture. In the Navajo tradition, it comes down to 3 values: Woshdee, Bahozho, and K’enidzin.

item.title: Tribal people can now confidently and safely trade goods and services worldwide
item.description: Tribes.Humans.Net is a new platform we created as a peer to peer network to enable inter tribal trade within our communities and outside.

item.title: Refueling our souls with a tribal dacha
item.description: As an honorable tribal person searching for a strong foundation of family, we value a home in the community where we grew up. This enables us to maintain ties to the earth and family.

item.title: In the Mind of a Bull Rider
item.description: Bull riding, America’s fastest growing sport, one of America’s most dangerous sports, and one of Native America’s biggest sports.

item.title: Success with Harmony: Rise early, pray, grind, and grow always
item.description: You may ask yourself what does it take to succeed? There are many self help gurus in our world all offering good strategy from their experiences.

item.title: Creativity is what makes the Planet go round
item.description: To the Creative: Do what you love, enjoy what you do, make life worth it. It’s very cliché but it’s true.
